value.rationale: Sharp affine least-squares stability under removing a concentric hole is a natural geometry-dependent design issue absent from the filled-ball and sphere endpoint theories. The result supplies an exact computable norm for every hole size, complete row maximizers, a strict global monotonicity theorem with a distribution-order proof, a sharp small-hole coefficient proportional to deleted volume, and a uniform high-dimensional law. These jointly quantify how a macroscopic topological/geometric change improves worst-case approximation stability; the all-radius assertion is not a routine isolated numerical slice.
